definition: Articulation, in vocal speech, is the coordinated action of the larynx and mouth that shapes or interrupts the flow of breath to produce distinct speech sounds. These sounds depend on both the noises made as breath passes the speech organs and the resonance created by the shape of the mouth and nose.
